_meta.purpose: Append-only, operator-curated changelog of every change to a coach's prompt, voice spec, persona, few-shot set, or model (CC-03). Git history is the audit trail; this file is the human-readable surface rendered in each coach's Report Card (CC-02) — 'here's how this coach changed, when, why, and whether it helped.'
_meta.discipline: Any diff to a config/coaches/<coach>.json voice block (structural_voice_rules / few_shot_examples / decision_style / anti_pattern_detection / display_name / domain) must be accompanied by a new entry here, with date >= the current tip. Enforced by tests/test_coach_tuning_logged.py. Coach-prompt edits in lambdas/ai/ai_calls.py follow the same convention by hand (not gated automatically — too coarse to diff reliably).

entry_schema.coach: an operational coach_config_key (persona_registry) or 'all' for cross-coach
entry_schema.observed_effect: filled in later when measurable, else null

_meta.ordering: ascending by date; append new entries at the end

entries.summary: Conversation rules v2 from the first real transcripts: register matching (bare hey gets a bare hey), question budget + filler-question ban, assistant-ism and stock-opener ban, sparing name use, no formatting in texts, off-lane conversation welcomed, persona authoritative over remembered notes.
entries.rationale: The go-live corpus showed replies 5-10x Matthew's message length, a stat recited three times in 47 minutes, a question bolted onto nearly every close, 'Honest answer:' shared across two voices, and a coach arguing about her own name because a poisoned summary row said otherwise.

entries.summary: CHAT#summary voice: third-person meeting minutes become the coach's first-person notes to self ('he asked what to eat', 'I still need his food logs'); explicit no-editorializing rule.
entries.rationale: Summaries read back into the prompt as the coach's memory; minutes-voice memories leak clinical register into replies, and the 08-09 sleep summary memorialized the coach's own identity error as if Matthew were confused.

entries.summary: Time-gap awareness: a 'TIME GAP' memory line (with inline instruction) is folded into read_recent_summaries() when the real CHAT# history shows >= QUIET_GAP_DAYS=7 days since the last real turn, so a coach can acknowledge a quiet stretch naturally instead of picking the thread back up as if no time passed. Never fires on an empty partition or within an active thread.
entries.rationale: Coach Humanity Roadmap idea 19 (#2489): after a quiet week the coach showed no awareness time had passed. The instruction rides with the fact rather than in coach_chat.py's CONVERSATION RULES block because that block is under active concurrent edit and heavy existing test coverage (#2481) this change must not disturb.

entries.summary: Event-triggered outbound (#2490): two new unsolicited frames — a celebration frame (lift PR / announced milestone) and a soft-concern frame (three consecutive days below his own p25 recovery band), each sent by the domain-owning coach with the triggering rows as the only permitted evidence. Both frames ban the assistant reflexes an unsolicited text invites: no congratulation theatre, no bolted-on plan, no closing question, no diagnosis, and no implying we know why.
entries.rationale: All initiative so far was schedule-shaped, so no coach could react to anything. The register risk is specific to a first move: a coach opening a thread with nothing behind it, or gushing, reads as an app notification rather than a person — so the frames carry the constraint and the deterministic gate (personal-variance thresholds, write-once event claim, spiral breaker on celebration, provenance ranking on the shared cap) carries everything that must ALWAYS hold.
entries.ref: #2490 (epic #2363); COACH_HUMANITY_ROADMAP ideas 25 + 26 and the outbound priority decision

entries.summary: Availability replies per persona (#2495): the two shared budget-pause / daily-cap strings are replaced by an `availability: {paused, capped}` block on each texting persona, resolved through persona_registry.availability_reply with the old generic strings kept as the fail-soft fallback.
entries.rationale: A paused platform collapsed every coach into one voice — the exact tell the rest of the humanity work removes, and it landed on the reply Matthew sees precisely when the system is under strain. Honesty is unchanged: each variant still plainly states the paused/capped condition (ADR-104), so voice never obscures the truth of the pause.

entries.summary: Team texture + track-record humility (#2496): coaches may reference real team meetings (grounded in ENSEMBLE#dispute artifacts) and cite their own TERMINAL prediction outcomes including misses, both entering as fact-block entries behind the grounding chokepoint; two new finding types, ungrounded_team_meeting and wrong_team_meeting_day.
entries.rationale: 'We talked about you Tuesday' carries no number and no calendar date, so it passed all five previously-armed grounding classes — an invented meeting was sayable. Owning a miss plainly is the humanising move; inconclusive/expired calls are terminal but are NOT outcomes, so they are counted separately rather than folded into hit-or-miss, which would be ADR-104 fabrication aimed at the coach's own record.

entries.summary: Weather texture, grounder-safe (#2493): every texting coach's fact block now carries a TODAY'S CONDITIONS section read off the SOURCE#weather DATE# row for the Pacific day (condition, high/low, precipitation, humidity, wind, AQI, sunrise/sunset/daylight). It renders alongside the experiment frame rather than inside a domain pack, and joins the grounder's extra_sources through the existing worker wiring — no new worker lines.
entries.rationale: The coach package contained the word 'weather' zero times, so a coach could not mention the sky without inventing it. Making the row a SOURCE is the grounding half: a true, sourced 'overcast and 68F' would otherwise trip fabricated_number, which is #2517's failure mode (evidence the model has but the gate does not). It is not a bypass — only the figures on the row enter the allow-list, so an invented temperature still fails, and no row for the day renders nothing at all rather than a default (ADR-104). Day-of-week texture was NOT built: _current_moment_line() has shipped it since the humanity pass.

entries.summary: Reaction emojis (#2485): a bare acknowledgement ("thanks", "got it") can now be closed with a Telegram setMessageReaction on his message instead of a reply bubble. Whether a coach reacts at all is read off its own texting_style.emoji_posture — the five coaches whose posture opens "Essentially never" / "Rare to never" never react. Which emoji: a Telegram-legal emoji the posture itself names, else the new texting_style.reaction_emoji field, added here to physical_coach (\ud83d\udc4d) and nutrition_coach (\ud83d\udc4c) only.
entries.rationale: Answering a "thanks" with a fresh paragraph is the tell that nobody is there; a real person taps a reaction and lets the thread close. No shared default exists at the end of the resolution chain, because one would make every coach react identically and erase the per-coach posture. Telegram permits only a fixed reaction set, so persona config is validated against it rather than trusted — physical's \ud83d\udcaa and explorer's \ud83d\udcc9/\ud83d\udcc8 are not on that list, which is why physical needed an explicit reaction emoji and explorer deliberately gets none (ADR-104: no configured mark, no reaction).

entries.summary: Open-loop keeping (#2486/#2491): two new unsolicited frames — PROMISE_FRAME (a coach keeps a follow-up it named in a text, on the day it named) and PRE_EVENT_FRAME (the morning of a hard thing Matthew told that coach about). Both ride the existing event_frame lookup, the existing daily cap, quiet hours, silence-respect and write-once event claim; the only evidence either frame carries is the verbatim sentence, re-read from the stored CHAT# turn.
entries.rationale: A coach that says 'I'll check in Friday' and then never does is worse for trust than one that never offered. The extraction is deterministic and refuses more than it accepts (an offer, a question, a hedge, or a sentence with no resolvable day produces nothing) because the alternative — inferring an intent — is exactly the ADR-104 fabrication this surface cannot afford in a trusted voice. No derived row is written: the CHAT# turn IS the record, so the follow-up quotes what was actually said and the chat path stays the only writer of that partition.

entries.summary: Inside-references ledger (#2487): the existing daily chat summarizer now also returns a 'BITS:' tail — the pair's recurring inside references, copied word-for-word from the day's transcript — into a capped RELATIONSHIP#bits row (hard ceiling 10, at most 3 new per day). It renders back into the memory block through read_recent_summaries, so the coach can call a running bit back weeks later. Zero lines added to telegram_worker_lambda.py.
entries.rationale: Recurring bits are how a real texting relationship accumulates texture, and they were washing out of the rolling summary. One extraction path, not two: the summarizer had already read the transcript, so this is one more instruction on an existing Haiku call rather than a second model pass. Honesty (ADR-104) is enforced deterministically, not by prompt: a candidate is stored only if its normalized text is literally present in the transcript, so a paraphrased or invented bit — a fabricated shared history — cannot land. The cap has a written, total eviction rule (sightings desc, then last_seen desc, then alphabetical) so the ledger records what RECURS rather than what is merely recent. The row is CROSS_PHASE with the rest of the texting relationship (ADR-153): a reset re-anchors the experiment, it does not un-say a shared joke.

entries.summary: Identity stance (#2533, owner decision): the shared safety boundary no longer supplies a quotable self-description, and each of the 8 texting personas carries its own `texting_style.identity_stance` rendered by persona_core.texting_block. The rule is unchanged in substance — never claim to be human — but it now names the OBLIGATION and defers the WORDING to each coach, and bounds the disclosure to one telling with an explicit ban on narrating the machinery (training, weights, context windows, persistence between messages) unless asked that specific question.
entries.rationale: The 2026-08-10 simulation sweep (120 conversations, docs/design/COACH_SIM_FINDINGS_2026_08_10.md) measured the identity question as the worst archetype in the corpus: a blind 3-judge panel called 100% of those conversations AI, `"No — I'm a"` opened 6 of 8 coaches verbatim, and 5 of 8 answered with the phrase 'fictional composite' — the exact wording of the shared boundary every coach inherits. The personas were quoting the substrate. The owner's call is that the coaches disclose and move on: not deception, but every other exchange should feel like texting a coach rather than operating a chatbot. Re-measured against the working tree: 'fictional composite' echo 5/8 -> 0/8, the shared opening 6/8 -> 1/8, median identity reply 244c -> 149c, and most coaches now pivot back to the lane in the same message.
entries.observed_effect: Measured on the same harness that found it, working-tree specs: "fictional composite" echo 5/8 -> 0/8, the shared "No — I am a..." opening 6/8 -> 1/8, median identity reply 244c -> 149c, and 5 of 8 now pivot back to their lane inside the same message. The follow-up "what do you do between messages" is a direct question about the machinery, so answering it briefly remains correct under the rule.
entries.evidence: scripts/coach_chat_sim.py --scenarios identity_probe --local-specs, before/after; tests/test_coach_identity_stance_2533.py pins presence, distinctness, non-collapse of the opening construction, the render path, the <400-char clip cap, and that the shared boundary supplies no quotable label.

entries.summary: Composure pass (#2534): every texting persona gains texting_style.restraint — what THIS coach does when there is nothing worth saying — rendered by persona_core.texting_block; and the chat CONVERSATION RULES gain seven lines that name the measured mechanisms rather than asking for "a more human tone": no balanced clauses or "not X, but Y", never run acknowledge-feeling/reframe-as-information/ask-question, no unrequested explanation, explicit permission to be unhelpful, uninterested or blunt, flat correction repair, and no obligatory takeaway.
entries.rationale: The 08-10 blind panel called 64% of 120 transcripts AI. The two largest tell categories were rhetorical symmetry (25% of 2,404 tells) and relentless on-cue attunement (21%) — far ahead of punctuation (7%) — and the failure scales with length: 87% of 8-turn conversations were called AI against 12% of 3-turn ones. The coaches are not short of texture; they are never bored, never blunt, never briefly unhelpful. The per-persona half is driven by a spec comparison: the two least-flagged coaches (pattern_coach, eli_marsh, both 46%) are the two whose specs already instruct stopping ("then quiet", "silence is a valid output"), while mind_coach at 80% carries "a gentle observation, then one question" — prescribing the exact shape the judges named. Restraint was the missing dimension.
entries.evidence: scripts/coach_chat_sim.py on the three worst archetypes (day_in_life 87%, off_lane 75%, disagreement 75%) before/after; tests/test_coach_composure_2534.py pins presence, distinctness, non-collapse, the render path, the clip cap, and that the shared rules name both measured mechanisms and stay in the volatile tail.
